draft.title: Ecological footprint
card: An ecological footprint measures the area of land and water needed to supply what a person, city or country uses. It also covers the area needed to absorb the waste they produce.
It is counted in global hectares, which allows different places to be compared. A larger footprint means a greater demand on the Earth's natural resources.
Rich countries tend to have much larger footprints per person than poorer countries. People in them generally use more food, energy, goods and transport.

A footprint can be compared with biocapacity, which is the amount of land and water that can renew resources and absorb waste. If a footprint is larger than this, resources are being used faster than they can be replaced.
draft.remember: A footprint is the land and water a lifestyle needs, and wealthy countries usually need much more.

a.q: Which of these does a country's ecological footprint measure?
opts: The land and water needed to supply its use and absorb waste
The total area of land that lies inside its borders
The amount of money spent on protecting its environment
The number of species that live in its national parks
a.why: A footprint measures the land and water needed to meet what people use and to absorb their waste. Land inside borders is tempting, but a footprint can be bigger or smaller than a country's actual area.
a.clue: Think about the area needed to supply and absorb, not the area owned.

b.q: Country X is wealthy and Country Y is poor. Both have similar populations. Which result is most likely, and why?
opts: X has a larger footprint, as its people use more resources
Y has a larger footprint, as its people use more resources
X has a smaller footprint, as it has more land to use
Y has a smaller footprint, as it has more land to use
b.why: Wealthy countries generally have much larger footprints per person because their people use more food, energy and goods. The tempting wrong answers treat the footprint as the size of land owned, but it measures the area needed to meet use and absorb waste.
b.clue: Footprint follows how much people use, not how much land a country has.

a.best: The land and water needed to supply its use and absorb waste

b.best: X has a larger footprint, as its people use more resources
